newsitem.title: PERU: Colombian hostage-taker in Lima to debate crisis.
newsitem.headline: Colombian hostage-taker in Lima to debate crisis.

text.p: A former Colombian guerrilla leader who masterminded the 1980 Dominican Embassy siege in Bogota arrived in Peru early on Monday to take part in a seminar on the Lima hostage crisis.

Rosemberg Pavon, the former "Comandante Uno" ("Commander One") of the M-19 rebels, gave away no secrets in reply to reporters' questions on how to end the three-month-old crisis in which Marxist guerrillas are holding 72 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence.
"I do not give advice to either party," he said when asked how he would recommend ending the standoff between Peru's government and the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA).

He did say, however, that he disagreed with the MRTA, whose Dec. 17 takeover of the residence has overtaken his 61-day operation in Bogota as the longest hostage siege in Latin America's turbulent guerrilla history.
"I am in agreement with democracy," said Pavon, who now works as an academic and adviser to local governments in Colombia.

In a drama strikingly similar to the Lima crisis, Pavon's 15-strong M-19 commando unit held 57 hostages -- including 19 diplomats -- at the Dominican Embassy in Bogota for 61 days before taking $2 million and a plane to Cuba.
Peru's hostage-takers number about 20, hold a handful of diplomats among their 72 hostages, and have also been offered asylum by Cuban President Fidel Castro.
But Pavon insisted parallels should not be drawn between the two hostage sieges.
"I do not see similarity between one operation and the other. They are different events, two contexts and two distinct countries," he said.
Pavon will join intellectuals, journalists, former hostages and diplomats at the two-day seminar in Lima starting Tuesday.
